annotation.title_clean: Encoding the Enforcement of Safety Standards into Smart Robots to Harness Their Computing Sophistication and Collaborative Potential: A Legal Risk Assessment for European Union Policymakers
annotation.title_en: Encoding the Enforcement of Safety Standards into Smart Robots to Harness Their Computing Sophistication and Collaborative Potential: A Legal Risk Assessment for European Union Policymakers
annotation.summary_en: Peer-reviewed article arguing that EU occupational health and safety rules and international standards inadequately address smart collaborative robots (SmaCobs). It proposes encoding OHS enforcement directly into SmaCobs, possibly using quantum computing. It also discusses legal personality, how liability should be shared, and explainability, and calls for a new binding EU OHS Regulation.
key_provisions_or_claims: Current standards and EU/Member State laws fail to address physical and mental health risks of human-robot interaction with smart cobots
Machine learning makes smart cobots' behaviour opaque and hard to foresee, which adds to general HRI risks
Encoding OHS enforcement into smart cobots could be safer and more cost-effective than human enforcement
Raises issues of robot legal personality, how liability is shared, and algorithmic explainability
Proposes a new binding EU OHS Regulation for the smart cobot era
